props.title: Catalyst for synthetic-methanol production

props.name: difficultly reducible oxide(s) + cobalt oxide + metallic halide catalyst

evidence.quote: As illustrative of our invention we will cite two specific catalysts containing cobalt.
1. A methanol catalyst initially compris ing a plurality of difficultly reducible metal oxides, cobalt oxide, and a metallic halide.

props.name: Example I: cobalt hydrate on zinc oxide with zinc chloride

evidence.quote: 2250 grams of cobalt nitrate (Co(NO)- 6HO) are dissolved in 250 liters of water and the solution is heated to 95° C.
There is then added 7.5 kilograms of zinc oxide after which the solution is vigorously stirred and sufficient ammonium hydroxide is added to precipitate the cobalt as cobalt hydrate.
The precipitated mass is recovered by de cantation and filtration, is washed, dried, and broken up into granules.
The granules are then moistened with a solution contain ing 1480 grams zinc chloride and dried once

props.name: Example II: as Example I with magnesium bromide in place of zinc chloride

evidence.quote: If the zinc chloride in Example I is re placed by 1300 grams of magnesium bro mide the hourly yield of condensate and percentage yield of methanol is not greatly modified.

props.name: non-reducible oxide + easily reducible oxide + metallic halide catalyst

evidence.quote: We have now discovered a new type of valuable methanol catalyst which comprises three main elements-i.e.
(1) One or more non-reducible metal ox ides such as zinc, magnesium, cadmium, chromium, vanadium, tungsten, etc.;
(2) One or more easily reducible metal oxides such as copper, silver, iron, nickel, cobalt, etc.;

props.name: effects of space velocity, pressure and CO

evidence.quote: For example, an increased space velocity produces an increased hourly yield and an increase in operating pressure has the same effect.
Likewise the use of pure carbon monoxide as distinguished from carbon di oxide or a mixture of the two results in an increased methanol percentage in the con densate
but the results will always be proportionate to the catalyst employed.

props.statement: Increased space velocity and increased operating pressure increase the hourly yield; pure carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide or a mixture increases the methanol percentage in the condensate and the condensate volume; results are always proportionate to the catalyst employed.

props.name: carbon oxides and hydrogen react above 50 atm and 250 °C

evidence.quote: substance comprising metals or their oxides
at a pressure above 50 atmospheres and at a
temperature above 250° C. there is nearly always produced some reaction between the gaseous components.

props.statement: When carbon oxides with excess hydrogen are passed over a catalytic substance of metals or their oxides at a pressure above 50 atmospheres and a temperature above 250 °C some reaction nearly always occurs; its extent depends on space velocity, temperature and pressure, and the products depend almost entirely on the nature and activity of the catalyst.

props.name: halide amount need not be exact; preferably < 1 equivalent

evidence.quote: To produce our improved catalysts it is not necessary that the amount of metallic halide added bear any exact weight relation to the remaining constituents of the cata lyst
though the amount of halide added should preferably be less than one chemical equivalent of the amount of principal me tallic oxide present in the catalyst.

props.statement: The amount of metallic halide need not bear any exact weight relation to the other constituents, though it should preferably be less than one chemical equivalent of the principal metallic oxide.

props.name: halide catalysts better than identical catalysts without halide

evidence.quote: In these cases however, our improved catalysts containing halides produce far better results than those known in the art for otherwise identical catalyst mixtures.

props.statement: With easily reducible oxides such as those of copper or silver, the catalysts containing halides produce far better results than those known in the art for otherwise identical catalyst mixtures.

props.name: methanating metals serve advantageously in the halide catalysts

props.statement: In the improved catalyst compositions the normally deleterious methanating metals iron, nickel or cobalt serve advantageously, apparently exerting only a normal hydrogenating catalytic action productive of methanol.

props.name: iron, nickel, cobalt oxides described as worthless (prior art)

evidence.quote: In the past, also, one class of easily re ducible metal oxides, that is the oxides of iron, nickel, and cobalt have been described as absolutely worthless for the production of methanol catalysts since these metals un der normal conditions prevent the formation of methanol

props.note: cited from the prior art; the patent argues against it
props.statement: In the past the oxides of iron, nickel and cobalt have been described as absolutely worthless for methanol catalysts, since these metals under normal conditions prevent the formation of methanol, the reaction producing only methane.

props.name: two principal types of prior methanol catalysts

evidence.quote: 1. Mixtures of finely divided metals, or, what is equivalent, mixtures of easily re ducible metal oxides;
2. Mixtures of oxides of metals non-re ducible, or difficulty reducible under the con ditions of the methanol synthesis.

props.statement: Methanol catalysts proposed in the past were of two principal types: mixtures of finely divided metals (or easily reducible metal oxides), and mixtures of oxides of metals non-reducible or difficultly reducible under the synthesis conditions.

props.name: carbon monoxide seems to react more readily

evidence.quote: and, since carbon monoxide seems to react more readily, an increased conden sate volume.

props.statement: Carbon monoxide seems to react more readily than carbon dioxide, giving an increased condensate volume.

props.name: halide forms oxychloride compounds

evidence.quote: The precise method by which the metallic halides produce the improvement is not known to us.
(2) The metallic halide interacts with other metallic oxides present in the catalyst to produce oxychloride compounds which, in turn, either serve as catalyst promoters

props.statement: The metallic halide interacts with other metallic oxides in the catalyst to produce oxychloride compounds which either serve as promoters or modify the physical state of the mass to give a more active catalyst.

props.name: halide acts as an ordinary promoter

evidence.quote: The precise method by which the metallic halides produce the improvement is not known to us.
(1) The metallic halide acts as an ordi nary "promoter” in increasing catalyst ac tivity;

props.statement: The metallic halide acts as an ordinary promoter in increasing catalyst activity.

props.name: halide reduced to finely divided metal

evidence.quote: The precise method by which the metallic halides produce the improvement is not known to us.

(3) The metallic halide may be reduced by the high pressure contact with hydrogen and carbon oxides during the commencement of its use as a catalyst and the resultant finely divided metal may increase the cata lyst activity

props.statement: The metallic halide may be reduced by the high-pressure contact with hydrogen and carbon oxides at the start of use, and the resulting finely divided metal may increase activity; or the halide may first react with another metal to give its halide, which is reduced in the same way.
